comments.body:
PRE-IMPLEMENTATION INVENTORY — a convergence decision is required before any code is written, because the three copies are NOT interchangeable and no merge leaves the pinning tests green.

THE BLOCKER (finding 8.2). For an inadmissible reason the CLI REFUSES (exit 1, transition.py:569-587 _plain_reason_refused, pinned by test_administrative_close_dispositions.py:343 and :352) while the library SILENTLY DISCARDS it (returns 0, _lib_writes.py:314-337 admits_close_reason, pinned by test_library_close_reason_is_gated_on_the_admitting_class:262-289 asserting seen['close_reason'] == ''). A shared reason_refusal() must pick one. Refusing uniformly breaks the library test; discarding uniformly breaks both CLI tests. This asymmetry is load-bearing on both sides.

DECISION RECORDED: converge on the CLI's REFUSE. Silently accepting a datum and never reading it is precisely the defect class bug defiant-orthoclase-buck was filed for (txn.py:263-273), and this ticket's own Context cites it. A library caller who passes a reason that cannot be persisted should learn that, not be ignored. This is a deliberate behaviour convergence under the parent epic's convergence clause, NOT a silent one: the library gains a rejection it did not have, and test_library_close_reason_is_gated_on_the_admitting_class must be updated to assert the refusal rather than the silent discard. That is a sanctioned assertion edit and must be called out in the change.

FOUR MORE TRAPS the implementation must respect:
- 8.7 (worst): close_disposition.verdict fails closed on an empty reason (close_disposition.py:200-201). If a normalised ''->'(no reason given)' placeholder ever reaches it, an UNJUSTIFIED disposition acquires a SIGNATURE. The placeholder must never flow into verdict().
- 8.3: a bare --force gives force_reason='' which is FALSY at txn.py:232's 'not (close_reason or force_close_reason)'. It works today only because _force_note converts ''->placeholder BEFORE close_ticket. If TransitionRequest.force_note is lazy, or the normalisation moves relative to the refusal, 'transition <id> in_progress closed --class=obsolete --force' flips from accepted to REFUSED.
- 8.5/8.6: force DISQUALIFIES the reason upstream but SATISFIES the reason-requirement at txn.py:232. close_reason, force_note and reason_refusal() must stay three independent accessors; conflating them re-opens that.
- 8.9: _lib_writes.transition(force_close=) is a DEPRECATED PUBLIC ALIAS while close_ticket(force_close=) is an internal hop name. Same spelling, unrelated. A mechanical rename silently retires the public deprecation shim.

Also: the guard as specified in AC-2 (literal in an assignment/return expression) MISSES _lib_writes.py:412, where the placeholder is produced as a call-argument expression. Five code sites, not four reachable by that scan shape.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
UNPARENTED FROM EPIC 2ddd AND CLOSED — this is not a consolidation.

The pre-implementation inventory established that the three 'copies' of the close-reason/force rule are not copies at all. They differ in four material ways: the CLI checks target_status == 'closed' and the library does not; the CLI reduces force to a bool while the library tests identity on str|None and the engine tests truthiness; empty-reason handling differs at each layer; and most decisively the CLI REFUSES an inadmissible reason (exit 1) where the library SILENTLY DISCARDS it (returns 0). Both dispositions are pinned by tests, so there is no merge that leaves the suite green — converging either way is a deliberate behaviour change, not a de-duplication.

That is disqualifying for this epic specifically. The parent's consolidation guarantee is that no consolidation child changes a PINNED observable behaviour and that the net non-test line count is negative. 825c would change pinned behaviour on at least two surfaces (the library gains a rejection it never had; MCP gains a 'reason' parameter it has never accepted, flipping a strict-xfail) and is net additive. It is a behaviour-converging API change plus an MCP feature, and grouping it with the mechanical collapses would have made the epic's own acceptance criteria untruthful.

The analysis is NOT lost: the inventory comment above records the four asymmetries with file:line citations, the convergence decision and its rationale, and four implementation traps — including that normalising an empty reason into the '(no reason given)' placeholder would let close_disposition.verdict turn an UNJUSTIFIED disposition into a SIGNED one, and that a bare --force flips from accepted to refused if that normalisation moves relative to the refusal check at txn.py:232. Anyone picking this up should start from that comment.

Closed by operator decision as out of scope for the consolidation epic.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The close-reason and force plumbing is computed independently on each surface: the "reason persists only on a REASON_REQUIRED class without force" rule lives at `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:584`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:318`, and `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:357-362`; the `"(no reason given)"` placeholder at `transition.py:388`, `claim.py:38`, `_lib_writes.py:412`; one datum travels as `force_reason` → `force_close` → `force_close_reason` across three files. The CLI refuses an inadmissible reason while the library silently discards it, and MCP `transition_ticket` (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:224-232`) does not expose `reason` at all — the strict-xfail row in `tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py:34-35,193` (bug `scratchy-leprous-galago`). Bug `defiant-orthoclase-buck` was the datum accepted under one name and never read.

## Approach
Add `src/rebar/_commands/transition_request.py` with a frozen `TransitionRequest(ticket_id, current, target, close_class, reason, force, caused_by, ref)` exposing `force_note`, `close_reason`, and `reason_refusal()`. All three surfaces construct it; `txn.transition_core` and `close_ticket` read the properties. MCP `transition_ticket` gains `reason` by constructing the same object, which flips the strict-xfail to a pass and forces its removal. Guard: the placeholder literal and the REASON_REQUIRED admission test appear only in `transition_request.py`.


## Guard construction
Follow the guard-test construction rule in the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: owner module exempt, match the constituent conjunction or AST shape named in Approach (or the definition count where no distinctive atom exists), `# <construct>-ok: <reason>` escape marker, and behaviour pinned only by the named existing tests.

## Scope
`src/rebar/_commands/transition_request.py` (new), `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/claim.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`, `tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py`, `tests/unit/commands/test_transition_request.py` (new).

## Testing
Happy path: each surface closing a REASON_REQUIRED class with a reason persists it. Edge: a reason on a non-reason class is refused identically on CLI, lib, and MCP (the parity oracle row). Pinning: `tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py`, `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py`, `tests/unit/test_administrative_close_dispositions.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp.py` pass unchanged except the removed xfail marker.


## The `(no reason given)` oracle, corrected (review remediation)
The earlier AC-2 demanded `grep -rn "no reason given" src/rebar` return exactly ONE file. That
cannot pass, and should not: the literal occurs **15 times across 5 files**, and only **5 are
code** —
- code: `_lib_writes.py:247`, `_lib_writes.py:412`, `_commands/transition.py:396`,
  `_commands/claim.py:43`, `_commands/claim.py:46`
- prose: `_deprecations.py:100` (a comment), `_lib_writes.py:235,238,278,385`,
  `transition.py:65,264,343,390` (docstrings and help text that legitimately NAME the value
  they document).

A guard that forbade documentation from naming the placeholder would be deleted the first time
someone wrote a docstring. So the construct is the **production of the value**, not the mention
of it: the placeholder becomes a single named constant on the value object
(`TransitionRequest.NO_REASON_GIVEN`), and the guard asserts the string LITERAL is assigned in
exactly one place under `src/rebar`, with a `# force-reason-ok: <why>` escape. Docstrings and
comments are out of the scan by construction (the scan looks for the literal in an assignment or
return expression, not anywhere in the line), so prose stays free.

`src/rebar/_commands/claim.py` IS added to Scope (two code sites above).
`src/rebar/_deprecations.py` is NOT added to Scope: its occurrence is a comment, and under the
corrected oracle it needs no change.

## Convergence decision (REQUIRED before implementation)
The three copies are not interchangeable and **no merge leaves every pinning test green**. For an
inadmissible reason the CLI **refuses** (exit 1, `transition.py:569-587`; pinned by
`test_administrative_close_dispositions.py:343,:352`) while the library **silently discards** it
(returns 0, `_lib_writes.py:314-337`; pinned by
`test_library_close_reason_is_gated_on_the_admitting_class:262-289`).

**Decision: converge on REFUSE.** Accepting a datum and never reading it is the exact defect class
of bug `defiant-orthoclase-buck` (`txn.py:263-273`), which this ticket's Context cites. The
library therefore gains a rejection it did not have, and
`test_library_close_reason_is_gated_on_the_admitting_class` is updated to assert the refusal
instead of the silent discard — a **sanctioned assertion edit**, recorded here under the parent
epic's convergence clause rather than made silently.

The library also gains the CLI's `target_status == "closed"` term, absent from
`admits_close_reason` and today saved only by a downstream guard (`txn.py:280-281`).

## Traps the implementation must not spring
1. **Never let the `(no reason given)` placeholder reach `close_disposition.verdict`.** It fails
   closed on an empty reason (`close_disposition.py:200-201`); a normalised placeholder there turns
   an UNJUSTIFIED disposition into a SIGNED one.
2. **Do not move the `""`->placeholder normalisation relative to the refusal check.** A bare
   `--force` yields `force_reason=""`, which is FALSY at `txn.py:232`; it works only because
   `_force_note` normalises before `close_ticket`. A lazy `force_note` flips a bare-force close
   from accepted to refused.
3. **`close_reason`, `force_note` and `reason_refusal()` stay three INDEPENDENT accessors.** Force
   DISQUALIFIES the reason upstream but SATISFIES the reason-requirement at `txn.py:232`.
4. **`_lib_writes.transition(force_close=)` is a deprecated PUBLIC alias**; `close_ticket(force_close=)`
   is an internal hop name. Same spelling, unrelated — a mechanical rename retires the shim.
5. Three tests pin NAMES/SOURCE TEXT and break on a signature change alone:
   `test_transition_core_does_not_accept_a_parameter_it_discards` (inspect.getsource),
   `test_adapter_bound_internals_are_not_contract_params`, and the
   `transition.transition_compute` spy reading `kwargs["close_reason"]`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One `TransitionRequest` carries the close-reason/force rule for CLI, library and MCP; checked by the guard test and the pinning suites.
- [ ] The `"(no reason given)"` placeholder is PRODUCED in exactly one place: a single named constant on the value object, with every one of the five current code sites (`_lib_writes.py:247,412`, `_commands/transition.py:396`, `_commands/claim.py:43,46`) reading it; checked by a guard asserting the string literal appears in exactly one PRODUCING expression under (assignment, return OR call-argument — `_lib_writes.py:412` produces it as a keyword-argument value, which an assignment/return-only scan misses) `src/rebar`, owner-exempt, with a `# force-reason-ok: <why>` escape whose reason is mandatory. **Docstrings, comments and help text that NAME the placeholder are explicitly out of the scan and must keep working** — there are ten such mentions and forbidding them would get the guard deleted.
- [ ] Pinning suites pass with no assertion edits; checked by `pytest` and `git diff --stat`.
- [ ] The library refuses an inadmissible reason exactly as the CLI does, and MCP does too; checked by the write-parity oracle with the `reason-close-obsolete` row passing on all three adapters and its strict-xfail marker deleted.
- [ ] A bare `--force` close of a reason-required class is still ACCEPTED; checked by a test driving `--class=obsolete --force` with no value.
- [ ] The placeholder never reaches `close_disposition.verdict`; checked by a test asserting an empty reason still yields no signed disposition.
